title: Fire
build: MAME's ROM set gnw_fire: fr-27, the Sharp SM5A's mask ROM of the Wide Screen Fire (FR-27), 1,856 bytes, CRC32 f4c53ef0, SHA-1 6b57120a0f9d2fd4dcd65ad57a5f32def71d905f, as MAME 0.289 lists it

records.c: wake: where the chip starts again after CEND, woken by a button of the selected row or by the 1 Hz flag. When no button of the row is down (it was the second that woke it), it asks for the screen to be drawn (set_redraw); then it makes a pass ($0004).

pass: one pass of the buttons, left and right, and the screen. It goes to read_keys ($0500) on page $14, which comes back to $0007, and calls read_pad ($03D6): a new press of left or right goes to pad_pressed ($02C7), and otherwise the pass goes on to draw_prep ($0600) through to_draw. Time is kept in after_draw and after_pass, not here.
to_draw: goes to draw_prep ($0600) on page $18, which comes back to after_draw ($0036).

after_pass: what to do once the screen is drawn. In a game, game_wait ($001D). Out of one: in the alarm's setting (mode bit 3) and after power on (mode 0), another pass; in the clock (mode 1), a second that has passed (tick_flags, $1A, bit 2) runs the demo's step ($0019), and otherwise the chip sleeps ($0030).
clock_second: the clock's demo, once a second: clears flag_06 ($06) bit 2 and goes to demo_step ($031E) on page $0C.

game_wait: in a game. Keeps time ($0200). While redraw_flags ($2B) bit 2 is set it makes another pass (that jump, $0021, never ran in a coverage run of every mode); while hold_count ($2A) is not 0 likewise ($0025, never ran). After the game is over (lcd_10 bit 2, the third angel) it runs the smoke's step at once ($0397, through $0028); otherwise it copies delay ($49) into delay_left ($4A) and starts the wait before the next step (wait, $0386).

sleep: when nothing waits to be drawn, selects the R4 row of buttons (select_r4) and sleeps (CEND) until a button of that row or the 1 Hz flag wakes the chip at $0000. With a redraw waiting it makes another pass instead ($0031, which never ran: the drawing clears the request first).

after_draw: where draw_prep comes back. Keeps time ($0200, which also plays the sounds), makes another pass if something asked for a redraw meanwhile, then: when tick_flags ($1A) bit 3 says a press of left or right broke into the wait, the wait goes on where it was ($0386, through $003D); otherwise after_pass ($000F).

add_point: a catch's point, reached from catch_check ($0318, through $03B1) in a game. Reads the R3 row (select_r3): with its K3 or K4 down (A of 4 or more, no pad on the board for either) the point is worth 2, otherwise 1 (the ADX $C skips the LAX 1, so the LAX 2 loads). Adds it to score_lo ($17); a digit that reaches 10 takes 10 off and carries into the next ($004B, the loop back to $0044 adds the carry), so the score runs in decimal. Past 999 it goes on to 000 ($004F, below). A carry that changes the hundreds ($0057 with BL = 5) goes to new_hundred ($005A). Then best_check ($006A).

past_999: when the hundreds carry too (BL reaches 4 after EXCD, and TABL with A = 4 skips), writes 9 to the units of a best score: best_a_lo ($47) when C from c_not_game_b is set and SBM chooses row 4, that is in Game A; best_b_lo ($27) in Game B, then the best check. The score itself is then 000.

new_hundred: a new hundred. When the hundreds digit is odd (skip_if_clear0 on score_hi), takes one from in_air ($09) (dec_count_09). Then, when the hundreds are 2 or 5 and a miss is shown (lcd_10 bit 1, the first angel), sets hold_count ($2A) to 10, the start of the bonus ($0067: bonus_hold then holds the game about six seconds and clears the angels).

best_check: compares the score ($15-$17) with the best of the game being played, digit by digit from the hundreds: best_a ($45-$47) when C from c_not_game_b is set and SBM chooses row 4, that is in Game A; best_b ($25-$27) in Game B. Equal digits go on to the next (EXCI 3 writes the digit back unchanged). At the first digit that differs, a score digit greater than the best's (ADDC without a carry) copies the whole score into the best (best_copy, $0080); otherwise nothing changes ($0079). Then jump_limit ($0088).
best_copy: copies score_hi, score_mid and score_lo into the best of the game being played (best_a or, in Game B, best_b), three EXCI 3 in a loop until BL reaches 8.

jump_limit: sets jump_limit ($19) to the score's tens digit plus one, at most 4 (tens of 3 or more give 4: the LAX 4 at $008D). Then the wait between steps: delay ($49) is 11 while the hundreds digit plus jump_limit is under 4; from 4 to 9 it is 14 less that sum; and 4 from 10 on (the LAX 3 at $009C, then ADX 1). So the game speeds up through each hundred's first thirty points and with each hundred, and the limit drops back to 1 at each new hundred. Then keeps time ($0200) and makes a pass ($0004), at $00A2, where the step's end also comes ($03AD, $0737).

tone_beep: waits for the divider's bits 11-14 to change, keeping the new reading in tone_div ($1B); then toggles the R pins with ATR from a counting A, R1 being the buzzer, and checks the divider again after each round of ATRs (A counted up to 16, once for each column from $1B down to $10): while it still reads tone_div the tone goes on, and when it has moved on the routine returns. So the tone lasts one step of those bits, 1,024 cycles, a sixteenth of a second (the divider counts two a cycle). Called by game_over_beeps ($01AD).

jump_chance: the step's first part, from $03AF. Works out C, whether someone jumps from the window this step. With no one in the air (in_air, $09, at 0), always ($00DC). With in_air at jump_limit ($19) or more, never. Otherwise, in a game ($00D1): never while stop_flags ($3B) bit 2 is set; always while twice in_air is less than jump_limit; else when the divider's bits 11-14 read under 4, four chances in sixteen ($00D9). In the clock ($00CC) the sum comes from stop_flags instead (ADD and ADDC on $3B).

miss_timer: while miss_time ($43) is not 0, a miss is being shown: takes one from it, and the step does nothing else (to after_draw, $00F4). At 7 it plays the miss's sound (sound_9); at 6 it goes to count_miss ($0197); at 2 it sets flag_07 ($07) bit 2 and asks for a redraw. At 0 the step goes on ($00F6).

step_turn: in a game, goes to turn_dispatch ($036D), which moves one part of the path. In the clock, sets turn_flags ($0A) bit 0 and clears bit 1, and goes to window_arc ($0158), from which the demo moves every part in one go.

arc3_move: moves the third arc one place on, by swaps along its chain with C clear at the start, so the place at the middle net empties: 1.1.0 (lcd_01 bit 1, on the middle net), 1.2.0, 4.0.0, 6.0.0, 7.0.0, then demo_firemen ($0340), then 0.1.0 and 1.3.0 (lcd_01 bit 3, above the right net). When someone has arrived above the right net, sets due_flags ($29) bit 2. In the clock it goes on to the demo's other arcs ($0131 and $0180); in a game to the drop from the lower window ($0117). Reached from turn_dispatch ($037C) and in the clock from $01F6 ($0103).

lower_drop: the jumper waiting at the lower window (2.0.1, lcd_12 bit 0, lit in Game B and in the clock's demo, never in Game A) drops into the first arc's last place before the left net (2.1.0, lcd_02 bit 1), and the step's click is asked for (sound_flags $20 bit 3), when all of these hold: hold_08 (lcd_08 bit 3, no segment) was clear (it is cleared here if set, and then nothing drops); the first arc's lower places 2.0.0, 2.1.0 and 2.2.0 are empty; and the seconds' units (secs_lo, $3B) have bit 3 set or in_air ($09) is odd. Then the end of the step's moves ($01C0).
to_arc4: in the clock, goes on to arc4_move ($0180). The SKIPs after it ($0133-$013E) are not reached.

turn_0_2: the step's turn when turn_flags ($0A) bit 0 is clear. With bit 1 clear (turn 0): sets bit 1 for the next step, then counts a miss if the person above the left net was never caught (due_flags bit 0: the left place 2.2.0 put out, the hurt figure 2.3.1 lit, and miss_start), and otherwise moves the middle arc (arc2_move, $01C3). With bit 1 set (turn 2): clears it and sets bit 0, counts a miss if the person above the right net was never caught (due_flags bit 2: 1.3.0 out, 1.2.1 lit, $0152), and otherwise moves the window and the first arc (window_arc, $0158).

window_arc: the first arc. C, from jump_chance, says whether someone jumps; but not while the window's place (3.3.1, lcd_13 bit 3) is still lit (RC). A jump adds one to in_air ($09) (count_up_09). Then swaps along the chain: 3.3.1, 3.3.0, demo_firemen ($0340), 2.0.0, 2.1.0, demo_firemen again, 2.2.0 (lcd_02 bit 2, above the left net). When someone has arrived above the left net, sets due_flags ($29) bit 0. In a game it takes whoever is above the right net (1.3.0) into arc4_move ($0180); in the clock it clears turn_flags bit 0, sets bit 1, and goes on to the middle arc ($01D9).

arc4_move: the last part of the path, from the right net to the ambulance: swaps C (whoever was taken from 1.3.0) along 0.1.1, 8.0.1 and 0.2.1. Whoever leaves 0.2.1 has reached the ambulance: in_air ($09) goes down one, and click_if_moved ($0265) asks for the step's click when anyone in the arc moved. In a game it then reads the R3 row: with K3 or K4 down (a test, no pads on the board) someone reaching the ambulance sets flags_0B ($0B) bit 3, plays sound $C and keeps time ($0192), and catch_check then gives the point; otherwise straight to catch_check ($01B6). In the clock, on to the third arc's lower drop ($01B8).

count_miss: from miss_timer when miss_time ($43) reaches 6. In a game, reads the R2 row, the test pads: with none down, shifts in one more angel (lcd_10 bits 1, 3 and 2: 8.1.1, then 8.3.1, then 8.2.1, the third ending the game). With a pad down (MAME's "Infinite Lives", R2 K1) the angel is not added and the miss beeps once ($019B, to $01A2). Sets hold_count ($2A) to 1, or to 5 when that was the third angel, clears the seconds' count ($40-$41), and then beeps that many times (game_over_beeps, $01A7).

game_over_beeps: while hold_count ($2A) is not 0: takes one from it, plays tone_beep ($00A6), writes sound $B to sound_21 and keeps time twice ($0200). Then clears sound_flags bit 0 and goes to catch_check ($01B6, $0300).
demo_to_arc3: in the clock, with C = bit 2 of the seconds' units (secs_lo, $3B), goes to the third arc's lower drop ($0117).

moves_done: the end of a game's moves from the third arc: click_if_moved ($0265) and catch_check ($02F9, $0300). In the clock, on to $01C3, the lower window's part of arc2_move, and from there to catch_check ($01D5).

arc2_move: outside Game A (mode bit 2 clear: Game B, and the clock's demo when it comes here from moves_done), first the lower window: hold_08 (lcd_08 bit 3) is set when C, from jump_chance, is set; and when 2.0.1 (lcd_12 bit 0) and the first arc's 2.0.0 and 2.1.0 are all empty, C puts a jumper at 2.0.1 and in_air ($09) counts it ($01D1). Then, in a game, the middle arc moves one place on, by swaps with C clear: 2.2.0 (above the left net), 2.1.1, demo_firemen, 3.2.0, 3.1.0, 4.3.0, 4.2.0, 4.1.0, demo_firemen, 1.0.0, 1.1.0 (above the middle net). When someone has arrived above the middle net, sets due_flags ($29) bit 1. Then moves_done's click and catch_check ($01EF). In the clock the middle arc is entered at $01D9, from window_arc, and after it the demo goes on to the third arc ($01F3); entered at the top, the clock goes from the lower window's part straight to catch_check ($01D5).
demo_to_arc3_move: in the clock, clears turn_flags ($0A) bit 1 and goes to the third arc ($0103). The SKIPs after it are not reached.

timekeep: called from after_draw ($0037), game_wait ($001E), the end of a point ($00A3) and between beeps ($01B0, $01B2). Without a new second (TG) it plays any sound waiting (play_sounds, $0280). On a new second, except after power on (mode 0): while the alarm rings (turn_flags, $0A, bit 2) and hold_count is 0 it asks for the alarm's sound (sound_flags bit 0); it sets tick_flags ($1A) bit 2, asks for a redraw, and adds one to the seconds' count ($40-$41). When that count passes 255 after a game is over (the third angel lit), it goes back to the clock: redraw_flags bit 3, mode 1, key_prev $E, and the tick cleared. Then adds a second to the time ($022D).

add_second: adds one to the seconds' units (secs_lo, $3B) and carries: past 9 into the tens (secs_hi, $3A), past 5 there into the minutes (minute_rolled, $026C). Entered at $0230 with B at a minutes' units cell and C set, it adds a minute the same way.
to_minute_rolled: the tens rolled over: goes to minute_rolled ($026C). The SKIPs after it are not reached.

add_hour: adds one to the hours at B ($37, or $33 for the alarm): 12 goes to 1, 9 to 10, and at 11 to 12 AM and PM swap (bit 3 of the tens). The same code as Parachute's and Octopus's ($0240 in games/gnw/parachute).

hour_from_minutes: from minute_rolled when the minutes' tens rolled over: swaps BL into A, so A is the column of the minutes' tens, and adds 8. For the time ($38) that carries and it goes to add_hour ($0240); for the alarm's minutes ($34) it does not, and $0263 goes to $0269, the alarm's hours. So the alarm's minutes, set past 59, carry into its hours. The coverage run did not set them past 59, so $0263 did not run there; it did on the model.

click_if_moved: asks for the step's click (sound_flags, $20, bit 3) when A is 0: a swap that found its place lit leaves A = 0 (swap's exit at $04C5), so after an arc's swaps A is 0 when anyone in it moved. Called after arc4_move ($0186) and moves_done ($01EF, $01F0). After it, $0269 points B at the alarm's hours ($33) and goes to add_hour's body ($0242), for left in the alarm's setting.

minute_rolled: the tens of seconds or of minutes rolled over. After the seconds (C clear), flags the minute for the alarm (flags_0B, $0B, bit 1) and adds a minute ($0230, with B at the minutes' units $39 and C set); after the minutes (C set), adds an hour ($0261).
add_minute: adds a minute to the time ($39), as right does when the time is set after power on.

sound_done: asks for a redraw, clears every sound request (sound_flags, $20) and returns from timekeep: the end of every sound. $027E clears the requests without the redraw ($0276). Before it, $027B points B at the alarm's minutes ($35) and goes into add_minute ($0272), for right in the alarm's setting.

play_sounds: the alarm's sound first (sound_flags bit 0): after power on and in the clock, and after a game is over (the third angel), it buzzes while the divider's bits 11-14 read under 4 ($028E, ATR from a counting A) and ends at sound_done; in a game under way the request is dropped. Otherwise, after power on and in the clock and in the alarm's setting the requests are cleared unplayed ($027E). In a game: while a redraw is waiting, only a numbered sound (play_numbered, $02C0); otherwise the catch (bit 2, a tone of length code $E, $02AD) before the step's click (bit 3, $029F: an EXBLA before each ATR swaps A and BL while BL counts down, so A takes turns between $B and the falling count and the buzzer moves several times, a short burst), and with neither, a numbered sound. Each ends at sound_done.

play_tone: a tone of length code A: the code goes into tone_div ($1B) and into BL; ATR with A counting from 0 to 15 (R1, the buzzer, changing at each), once for each BL from the code down to 0; then the code goes up one and the whole again, until it passes 15. So a lower code is a longer tone. Ends at sound_done ($0274).
play_numbered: takes the sound's number from sound_21 ($21), clearing it; 0 plays nothing; any other is played as play_tone's length code ($02B0).

pad_pressed: a new press of left or right. After power on (mode 0) left adds an hour ($0240) and right a minute ($0271), then a redraw and the screen ($02EA). In the alarm's setting (mode 8) it clears the seconds' count, and left adds an hour to the alarm ($0269) and right a minute ($027B); then a redraw and the step's body from jump_chance ($02E7). Otherwise: left moves the firemen one place left (firemen_left, $034F), right one place right (firemen_right, $0364), and both at once nothing ($02E3); then catch_check ($0300), so a press that brings the firemen under someone due is a catch.

catch_check: after every press of left or right and every step's moves. Where the firemen stand (2.2.1 left, lcd_12 bit 2; 1.1.1 middle, lcd_11 bit 1; otherwise right) it takes that place's bit of due_flags ($29) into C, clearing it (a swap with C clear): bit 0 left, bit 1 middle, bit 2 right. C set is a catch: sound_flags ($20) bit 2, the catch's tone, and through $0318 and $03B1 add_point ($0040) in a game, or a pass in the clock. The person stays lit above the net and goes on at the arc's next turn. With R3's K3 or K4 down (no pads for them on the board) C is not looked at: a point comes only when flags_0B ($0B) bit 3 is set, which arc4_move sets when someone reaches the ambulance, and it is cleared ($0315). So with that test key held the catches score nothing and each person who reaches the ambulance scores 2, as checked on the model. Without a catch, after_draw ($0036).

demo_step: the clock's demo, once a second (clock_second). Anyone still due above a net who was not caught falls: the place is put out and the hurt figure on the ground below it lit (2.3.1, 1.0.1 or 1.2.1, lcd_12 bit 3, lcd_11 bits 0 and 2), and for the left and middle ones in_air ($09) goes down one when the figure is lit (not for the right one). The left one ($0322) never ran in the coverage run. Then sets flag_07 ($07) bit 2, asks for a redraw and runs the whole step from the smoke ($0397).

demo_firemen: called in the middle of each arc's chain with C = whoever has just moved on from the place before the swap. In a game, or with C clear, it returns at once. In the clock, once a second (flag_06, $06, bit 2 set the first time), it moves the firemen toward the arc that is moving, by turn_flags ($0A): bit 0, the first arc, firemen_left ($034F); bit 1, the middle arc, to the middle ($0353); neither, the third arc, firemen_right ($0364). So the demo's firemen go where someone is about to land.

firemen_left: from the right (1.3.1, lcd_11 bit 3) to the middle (1.1.1, lcd_11 bit 1, at $0353, which also puts out the left firemen 2.2.1); from the middle or the left, to the left ($035A: 1.1.1 and 1.3.1 out, 2.2.1 lit).
demo_mid_or_right: for demo_firemen: turn_flags bit 1 set goes to the middle ($0353), clear to firemen_right.
firemen_right: from the left (2.2.1, lcd_12 bit 2) to the middle ($0353); from the middle or the right, to the right ($0369: 1.1.1 out and 1.3.1 lit).

turn_dispatch: one part of the path moves each step, by turn_flags ($0A) bits 0 and 1. With bit 0 set (turn 1) it clears it, then counts a miss if the person above the middle net was never caught (due_flags bit 1: 1.1.0 put out, the hurt figure 1.0.1 lit, miss_start), and otherwise moves the third arc (arc3_move, $0100). With bit 0 clear, turn_0_2 ($0140). So the turns run 0, 2, 1: the middle arc; the window, the first arc and the way to the ambulance; the third arc.

wait_spin: the body of one pass of the wait: from A = 6, ten rounds of INCBs from column 0 of row 0 until INCB skips at column 8, a fixed run of instructions that sets how long a pass of the wait takes.

wait: the wait before the next step. While delay_left ($4A) is not 0 it takes one from it and reads left and right (read_pad, $03D6): a new press sets tick_flags ($1A) bit 3 and goes to pad_pressed ($02C7), from which after_draw comes back here; otherwise it spins (wait_spin) and goes round. At 0, the step ($0393).

step: asks for a redraw. On turn 1 (turn_flags bit 0) the smoke moves first ($0397); otherwise, unless the game is over (lcd_10 bit 2), jump_chance ($00C0). After the game is over, a pass ($00A2) instead.

smoke: the smoke over the building, four puffs (3.2.1, 3.1.1, 3.0.1 in lcd_13 and 4.3.1 in lcd_14), moved by swaps: C, from bit 1 of the seconds' units (secs_lo, $3B), goes into 3.2.1, then on through 3.1.1 and 3.0.1 into 4.3.1. When none of the first three was lit before the move (A still 8 from the LAX, $03A3), 3.2.1 is lit anyway; when 4.3.1 was lit before, 3.2.1 is put out ($03A8). Runs on turn 1 of a game's step, every step after the game is over, and each second of the clock's demo. Then jump_chance ($00C0), in a game unless the game is over ($03AB), when it goes to a pass.
after_catch: in a game, add_point ($0040); otherwise keeps time and makes a pass ($00A2).
power_on: where the chip starts at power on and ACL: goes to power_setup ($0526) on page $14.

miss_start: a miss. One fewer in the air (dec_count_09), every due flag cleared (due_flags, $29), and miss_time ($43) set to 9 in a game (3 otherwise, $03C8, which never ran); miss_timer then holds the step for nine steps, counting the miss at 6 (count_miss). Then catch_check ($02F9).

read_pad: left and right. In the clock (mode bit 0) it returns at once. Neither, or both at once, clears tick_flags ($1A) bit 0, the held mark, and returns. One of them, newly pressed (bit 0 clear): sets the mark, keeps the divider's reading plus 4 in repeat_at ($28), and returns with a skip, a press. Held: in the clock and the games nothing; after power on, while the time is set (mode 0), and in the alarm's setting (mode 8, where ADX 9 at $03E9 carries), a press again each time the divider's bits 11-14, with bit 0 set, read repeat_at ($03EB), which then moves 4 on: a held button repeats every quarter second (those bits count sixteen a second). Live: 16 presses in 4 s.
clear_cell: writes 0 to the cell at B (LAX 0, EXC 0 at $0483).
clear_40_41: clears the seconds' count (secs_hi $40, secs_lo $41): B = $41, then clear_down.
clear_down: writes 0 to the cell at B and each one below it in the row, down to column 0 (LAX 0, EXCD in a loop until BL wraps; $0498 on page $12).
set_redraw: sets redraw_flags ($2B) bit 0, which asks for the screen to be drawn again. Entered at $0405 it sets bit 0 of whatever cell B points at.
ret_406: a lone RTN, where set_redraw returns.

draw_cell: shifts the cell at B into the screen's latches, by WS when its bit 3 is set and WR when it is clear (the latch takes A, the cell), and moves B on one column. The drawing ($0640) calls it once for each segment cell.
dec_count_09: takes one from count_09 ($09), stopping at 0 ($0480).
count_up_09: with C set, adds one to count_09 ($09) and returns A = 0; with C clear returns A = 8 and changes nothing ($048C).
c_not_game_b: points B at mode ($30) and returns with C clear when the mode is Game B (bit 1) and set otherwise ($0463).
skip_if_game: points B at mode ($30) and returns with a skip when the mode is Game B (bit 1) or Game A (bit 2) ($0474).
read_divider: A = the chip's divider, bits 11-14 (DTA, $0489).
skip_if_clear0: returns with a skip when bit 0 of the cell at B is clear ($04AD).
skip_if_clear1: returns with a skip when bit 1 of the cell at B is clear ($0440).
skip_if_clear2: returns with a skip when bit 2 of the cell at B is clear ($04A9).
skip_if_clear3: returns with a skip when bit 3 of the cell at B is clear ($04B9).
entry_418: a TRS that nothing calls.
skip_if_c: returns with a skip when C is set ($045C).

b_01: points B at lcd_01 ($01) ($046D). The entries after it point B at other cells the same way: b_02 ($041B), b_03 ($041C), b_04 ($041D), b_05 ($041E), b_06 ($041F) and b_08 ($0420), each through a jump into page $11, $12 or $13 (b_05 by $04EC to $04E2).
b_11: points B at lcd_11 ($11), an LBL and RTN in the table itself; b_12 ($0424) does the same for lcd_12 ($12).

select_r2: A = $D and ATR: R1 off and the R2 row of buttons, the test pads, selected; then read_row. select_r3 ($0429, A = $B) selects R3 and select_r4 ($042A, A = 7) the R4 row, Time, Game B, Game A and Alarm. Entered at $042B the R pins take whatever A holds, which is how the sounds toggle the buzzer (R1, bit 0).
read_row: A = the buttons of the selected row (KTA) and B = key_prev ($31) ($0468).
b_score: points B at score_hi ($15), the first of the score's three digits ($04B0).
skip_if_no_redraw: points B at redraw_flags ($2B) and returns with a skip when its bit 0, the request to draw, is clear ($04AC).
skip_if_l10_2: points B at lcd_10 ($10) and returns with a skip when its bit 2 is set ($045F).
take_bit0: when bit 0 of the cell at B is set, clears it and returns with a skip; when clear, returns ($0458).
take_bit1: the same for bit 1 ($04A5).
take_bit2: the same for bit 2 ($0470).
take_bit3: the same for bit 3 ($044C).
skip_if_mode_lt2: points B at mode ($30) and returns with a skip when the mode is 0 or 1 (power on or the clock) ($04B4).

sound_8: writes a sound's number to sound_21 ($21) for the sound routine to play: 8 here, 9 from sound_9 ($0437), $B from sound_b ($0438) and $C from sound_c ($0439), through $043A (LBL $21, EXC 0 at $04E5). A run of LAX loads only its first, so each entry loads its own number.

swap0: exchanges bit 0 of the cell at B with C ($04ED): afterwards the bit holds the old C and C the old bit, with A = 0. Called along a chain of segment cells, from its last place to its first, it moves every lit place one place on: this is how the figures walk. swap1 ($043C, $04D8), swap2 ($043D, $04CD) and swap3 ($043E, $04C0) do the same for bits 1, 2 and 3.
skip_if_clear1_body: TM 1, then RTNS when the bit is clear and RTN when set.
b_18_body: LBL $18, RTN. The SKIPs after b_02_body ($0449-$044B) are not reached.
b_02_body: LBL $02, RTN.
take_bit3_body: TM 3; when set, RM 3 and RTNS.
b_03_body: LBL $03, RTN. After it, $0456 and $0457 are the jumps that b_03 and b_08 enter by.
b_08_body: LBL $08, RTN.
take_bit0_body: TM 0; when set, RM 0 and RTNS.
skip_if_c_body: TC; RTNS when C is set, RTN when clear.
skip_if_l10_2_body: LB 1 ($10), TM 2, then RTN when bit 2 is clear and RTNS when set.
c_not_game_b_body: LB 3 ($30), RC, then TM 1, which skips the SC when mode's bit 1 is set: C is set unless the mode is Game B.
read_row_body: KTA, LBL $31, RTN.
b_01_body: LBL $01, RTN.
take_bit2_body: TM 2; when set, RM 2 and RTNS.
skip_if_game_body: LB 3 ($30); RTNS when mode's bit 1 or bit 2 is set, RTN otherwise. The jumps at $047B-$047E are entries of the call table that land on page $11's bodies.
dec_count_09_body: LB 4 ($09); when it is 1 or more, stores it less one; when 0, stores 0 ($0483, which clear_cell enters).
b_04_body: LBL $04, RTN.
read_divider_body: DTA, RTN.
count_up_09_body: with C set, adds one to count_09 ($09) and leaves A = 0 (the LAX 8 after LAX 0 is passed over); with C clear, A = 8.
jumps_496: two jumps, for take_bit1 ($04A5) and b_04 ($0486).
clear_down_body: LAX 0, EXCD 0, again until BL wraps from 0 to 15.
b_06_body: LBL $06, RTN, and the jump that b_06 enters by ($049F). The SKIPs at $04A0-$04A4 are not reached.
take_bit1_body: TM 1; when set, RM 1 and RTNS.
skip_if_clear2_body: TM 2; RTNS when clear, RTN when set.
skip_if_no_redraw_body: LB $E ($2B); skip_if_clear0's body follows at $04AD: TM 0, RTNS when clear, RTN when set.
b_score_body: LBL $15, RTN. The SKIP after it is not reached.
skip_if_mode_lt2_body: LB 3 ($30), LDA, ADX $E: a carry (mode 2 or more) skips the RTNS.
skip_if_clear3_body: TM 3; RTNS when clear, RTN when set. After it, the jumps for read_divider, skip_if_clear3 and clear_cell ($04BC-$04BE).
swap3_body: TM 3; a set bit is cleared, set again if C was set, and C set ($04C5, with A = 0); a clear bit is set if C was set and C cleared ($04C8). The other swaps share the two exits.
swap2_body: the same for bit 2.
swap1_body: the same for bit 1.
b_05_body: LBL $05, RTN.
set_sound_body: LBL $21, EXC 0: the sound's number into sound_21. Then the jumps for the sound entries and b_05 ($04E9, $04EC); the SKIPs at $04EA and $04EB are not reached.
swap0_body: the same as swap3_body for bit 0. The bytes after it ($04F7-$04FF: an LBL $43, LDA, TA0, RTNS, RTN and two jumps) never ran in the coverage run and nothing jumps to them.

read_keys: the R4 row, Time, Game B, Game A and Alarm, worth 1, 2, 4 and 8. Not read while a game is under way (it goes straight to the test pads, $0519), unless a game key is held (redraw_flags, $2B, bit 2) or the game is over (the third angel). With Alarm down the others are dropped (RM 2, 1, 0 on the reading). The reading goes into key_prev ($31); a change sets turn_flags ($0A) bit 3, asks for a redraw and clears the seconds' count ($40-$41); an unchanged reading with bit 3 set clears it and goes to mode_change ($0540). So a change counts when two readings in a row agree. Then the test pads ($0519, test_pads at $059D).
page14_unused: SKIPs that nothing reaches.

power_setup: from power_on ($03C0). Clears every data cell, row by row from column 12 down (clear_down from $4C, $3B, $2B, $1B and $0B), so the mode is 0; selects the R4 row; asks for a redraw; sets the time to 12:00 AM ($36 = 1, $37 = 2) and the alarm to 12:00 PM ($32 = 9, the tens' 1 and the PM bit, $33 = 2). Then keeps time and makes a pass ($0735, $00A2).

mode_change: a change of the R4 keys, agreed twice. Asks for a redraw. In the clock, any key stops the alarm ringing (turn_flags bit 2). With no key down: when a game key had been held (redraw_flags bit 2), the score is cleared ($0563): a game starts when its key is let go. With keys down: in a game under way they do nothing; otherwise the mode comes from their sum ($054D): 1 the clock (mode 1), 2 or 3 Game B (2), 4 to 6 Game A (4), 7 or more the alarm's setting (8). Coming from power on (old mode 0) it resets the divider and the 1 Hz flag (IDIV, TG), so the clock starts on a whole second. The same mode again outside the clock, and any new mode, asks for mode_setup (redraw_flags bit 3, $0572); every press that gives the alarm's setting (mode 8), from another mode or in the setting already, flips the alarm on or off (flags_0B, $0B, bit 2, $056F), except the first after power on, which takes the IDIV path. Then the test pads ($059D).
page15_unused: bytes after the last jump that nothing reaches: an LB, LAX, PTW, TAM and more LBs, never run in the coverage run.

alarm_minute: when a new minute has been flagged (flags_0B bit 1, from minute_rolled), clears it, and outside the alarm's setting: asks for a redraw, stops the ringing (turn_flags bit 2), puts out lcd_00 (the ambulance man and his bell), and, when the alarm is on (flags_0B bit 2), compares the alarm's four digits ($32-$35) with the time's ($36-$39, $058D): equal starts the alarm ($05A1). Then $05A8.

test_pads: reads the R2 row, pads not fitted on the board. K4 (A of 8 or more) rings the alarm at once ($05A1: turn_flags bit 2, the alarm's sound asked for, the ambulance man lit, lcd_00 bit 1); K3 (4 or more) puts the mode back to 0, as after power on, and clears the seconds ($05AF); K1 and K2 go on to alarm_minute ($0580). K1 also stops a miss being counted, but that is read at count_miss ($0199).
keys_done: when mode_setup was asked for (redraw_flags bit 3), clears the request and goes to mode_setup ($05C0); otherwise back to the pass ($0007).

mode_setup: clears rows 0 and 1 from in_air ($09) and jump_limit ($19) down, and $40-$43 (the seconds' count and miss_time); stops the ringing; puts the firemen at the left (2.2.1), and in the alarm's setting also lights 1.1.1 and 1.3.1, all three pairs; asks for a redraw; clears sound_21 and sound_flags, due_flags and hold_count, and flags_0B bit 0. In the clock and after power on: key_prev $E, tick_flags bit 2 and redraw_flags bit 2 cleared, and jump_limit 3; in the alarm's setting jump_limit 3 as well. In a game: the GAME A (2.3.0, lcd_02 bit 3) or GAME B (0.0.0, lcd_08 bit 0) label, redraw_flags bit 2 (the key is held: the game starts when it is let go), and jump_limit 0, so the first jumper is the one who jumps when no one is in the air. Then delay ($49) 11, and read_keys ($0500).

draw_prep: while the alarm rings (turn_flags bit 2), first the ambulance man's bell swings, from the divider ($0603). With no redraw asked for (redraw_flags bit 0), straight to undo_blanks ($0633, $0710). Otherwise, clearing the request: in a game with its key held, the best score of that game (best_a or best_b) is copied into the score's cells to be shown ($0617); in a game, game_screen ($0680). Out of a game ($0623): lcd_00 cleared and the bell (8.2.0, lcd_00 bit 2) lit when the alarm is on, unless it rings; then clock_screen ($06C0) in the clock and after power on, alarm_screen ($06E1) in the alarm's setting.

draw: shifts the segment cells into the latches: for the first common lcd_08 and lcd_01-lcd_04, then the three digits from score_hi-score_lo ($15-$17) through DTW, each with its extra segment from flag_05-flag_07 bit 0 (SMF when it is set), then lcd_00, and TW moves them to the first common; for the second, lcd_18, lcd_11-lcd_14 and the digits again. While hold_count is not 0 the angels' cell is drawn blinking: on odd counts only its bit 0 (8.0.1) is drawn ($0667); otherwise lcd_10 whole. Then the screen on (ATBP 1). When flag_07 bit 2 is set (at miss_time 2) it clears it and puts out the three hurt figures (1.2.1, 1.0.1, 2.3.1). Then undo_blanks ($0710).
game_screen: blanks the score's leading zeros (digit $B, DTW draws nothing) except the units. Then path_check ($0689).

path_check: looks at every place of the path, 2.1.1 and the lower window 2.0.1, the window 3.3.1, the way to the ambulance (8.0.1, 0.1.1, 0.2.1), lcd_01-lcd_04, flag_06 and flag_07 bit 0 (6.0.0, 7.0.0) and 0.1.0. When every one is out, in_air ($09) is set to 0 ($06B6), so a count left over can never stop the next jump. Then the drawing ($06B8, $0640).

clock_screen: after power on (mode 0) every segment cell is filled with $F, all lit ($06D1), and with an R3 key down ($06DA, a test) the second common is cleared and the score's cells set to 888. In the clock, with Time held (key_prev bit 0) the alarm's time is shown instead (alarm_screen, $06E1). Otherwise the time's digits ($37-$39) are copied into the score's cells ($06C5), and then am_pm ($06F3).

alarm_screen: lights the ambulance man (lcd_00 bit 1) and, unless lcd_00 bit 0 is lit, his arm (bit 3); copies the alarm's digits ($33-$35) into the score's cells. Then am_pm with the alarm's tens ($06F1); while the alarm rings it skips am_pm and goes to path_check ($06EF).

am_pm: with B at the hours' tens ($36 or $32): AM (4.1.1) or PM (4.2.1, lcd_14 bits 1 and 2) by its bit 3, the hours' 1 (4.0.1, lcd_14 bit 0) by its bit 0, and the colon (5.0.0, flag_05 bit 0). Then path_check ($0689) and the drawing.
am_pm_body: am_pm's AM or PM, the hours' 1 and the colon.

undo_blanks: turns the score's leading blanks ($B) back into zeros (ADX 5 carries only for 11 and up). Then: out of a game, after_draw ($0738, $0036); in a game while hold_count ($2A) is not 0, bonus_hold ($071C); while a game key is held (redraw_flags bit 2), a pass ($0735, through $00A2); otherwise after_draw.

bonus_hold: the bonus at 200 and 500 points with a miss shown. No step runs while hold_count is not 0: each pass in which the divider's bits 11-13 read 0 takes one from it and plays a tone of length code $B ($072B, into play_sounds at $02AE); when it reaches 0 the angels are cleared (lcd_10 bits 1 and 3, $072E). From 10 that took about six seconds on the model. $0725 never ran.
to_pass: keeps time and makes a pass ($00A2). After it, to_after_draw ($0738): after_draw ($0036). The SKIPs at the end are not reached.

lcd_00 ($00): latch 8, H1, the ambulance man. Bit 0 his arm down with the bell (8.0.0), bit 1 the man (8.1.0), bit 2 the bell up (8.2.0), bit 3 his arm up (8.3.0). The bell alone (bit 2) is the sign that the alarm is on.

lcd_01 ($01): latch 1, H1. Bit 0 the middle arc's last place before the middle net (1.0.0), bit 1 the place above the middle net (1.1.0), bit 2 the third arc's first place (1.2.0), bit 3 the place above the right net (1.3.0).
lcd_02 ($02): latch 2, H1. Bits 0 and 1 the first arc's last two places (2.0.0, 2.1.0), bit 2 the place above the left net (2.2.0), bit 3 the GAME A label (2.3.0).
lcd_03 ($03): latch 3, H1. Bit 0 has no segment and is not used; bits 1 and 2 the middle arc (3.1.0, 3.2.0), bit 3 the first arc's second place (3.3.0).
lcd_04 ($04): latch 4, H1. Bit 0 the third arc (4.0.0), bits 1-3 the middle arc (4.1.0, 4.2.0, 4.3.0).
flag_05 ($05): bit 0 the clock's colon (5.0.0, the first digit's extra segment).

flag_06 ($06): bit 0 the third arc's top (6.0.0, the second digit's extra segment). Bit 2 is set when the demo's firemen have moved this second (demo_firemen) and cleared each second of the clock (clock_second).

flag_07 ($07): bit 0 the third arc (7.0.0, the third digit's extra segment). Bit 2 asks the drawing to put out the hurt figures: set at miss_time 2 ($00F2) and by the demo ($033A), cleared by the drawing ($0675).

lcd_08 ($08): latch 0, H1. Bit 0 the GAME B label (0.0.0), bit 1 the third arc's last place before the right net (0.1.0). Bit 2 has no segment. Bit 3 has no segment either: hold_08, set in Game B when a jump is decided at the middle arc's turn ($01C8), and taken by lower_drop, which then lets no one drop from the lower window that step.

in_air ($09): how many people are on the path, from the window to the ambulance. One more for each jump (count_up_09), one fewer for each one who reaches the ambulance, at each miss, and at each odd hundred (new_hundred); set to 0 when no place of the path is lit (path_check).
turn_flags ($0A): bits 0 and 1 the step's turn (0, then 2, then 1: turn_dispatch); bit 2 the alarm ringing; bit 3 a change of the R4 keys seen once (read_keys).

flags_0B ($0B): bit 1 a new minute, for the alarm (minute_rolled sets it, alarm_minute takes it); bit 2 the alarm on; bit 3 someone reached the ambulance while R3's K3 or K4 is down (arc4_move), taken by catch_check for a point; bit 0 cleared by mode_setup.
lcd_10 ($10): latch 8, H2. Bit 0 the way to the ambulance (8.0.1). Bits 1, 3 and 2 the three angels of the misses, lit in that order (8.1.1, 8.3.1, 8.2.1): bit 2, the third, is the game over.

lcd_11 ($11): latch 1, H2. Bit 0 the hurt figure under the middle net (1.0.1), bit 1 the firemen at the middle (1.1.1), bit 2 the hurt figure under the right net (1.2.1), bit 3 the firemen at the right (1.3.1).

lcd_12 ($12): latch 2, H2. Bit 0 the jumper at the lower window, in Game B and the clock's demo (2.0.1); bit 1 the middle arc's first place (2.1.1); bit 2 the firemen at the left (2.2.1); bit 3 the hurt figure under the left net (2.3.1).
lcd_13 ($13): latch 3, H2. Bits 0-2 three puffs of smoke (3.0.1, 3.1.1, 3.2.1), bit 3 the jumper at the window (3.3.1).
lcd_14 ($14): latch 4, H2. Bit 0 the hours' 1 (4.0.1), bit 1 AM (4.1.1), bit 2 PM (4.2.1), bit 3 the fourth puff of smoke (4.3.1).

score_hi ($15): the score's hundreds, drawn by DTW on latch 5; with score_mid ($16) and score_lo ($17) the three digits the screen shows, in a game the score (the best while a game key is held), in the clock the time and in the alarm's setting the alarm. $B draws nothing (a blanked zero).
score_mid ($16): the score's tens. See score_hi.
score_lo ($17): the score's units. See score_hi.
lcd_18 ($18): latch 0, H2. Bits 1 and 2 the way to the ambulance (0.1.1, 0.2.1). Bits 0 and 3 have no segment and are not used.
jump_limit ($19): how many may be in the air before jump_chance stops the jumps: in a game the score's tens plus one, at most 4 (jump_limit at $0088), 0 when a game starts; 3 in the clock.
tick_flags ($1A): bit 0 left or right held (read_pad); bit 2 a second has passed (timekeep), for the clock's demo; bit 3 a press of left or right broke into the wait.
tone_div ($1B): the tone routines' count: the divider's reading in tone_beep, the length code in play_tone.
sound_flags ($20): the sounds asked for, played by play_sounds and cleared by sound_done. Bit 0 the alarm, bit 2 a catch, bit 3 the step's click.
sound_21 ($21): a numbered sound for play_numbered (sound_8 to sound_c), cleared when played.
best_b_hi ($25): the best score of Game B, hundreds; best_b_mid ($26) and best_b_lo ($27) the tens and units. Kept until power is lost: power_setup clears it.
best_b_mid ($26): see best_b_hi.
best_b_lo ($27): see best_b_hi.
repeat_at ($28): the divider's reading (bits 11-14, bit 0 set) at which a held left or right repeats while the time is set (read_pad).

due_flags ($29): someone has arrived above a net and must be caught before that arc's next turn: bit 0 the left, bit 1 the middle, bit 2 the right. catch_check takes the bit where the firemen stand; one left at the arc's turn is a miss.

hold_count ($2A): a count that holds the game up: the beeps of a miss (1) or of the game over (5, game_over_beeps), and the bonus at 200 and 500 points with a miss shown (10, new_hundred). While it is not 0 the alarm's sound is not asked for.
redraw_flags ($2B): bit 0 a redraw asked for (set_redraw), bit 2 a game key held since the game was set up (the game starts when it is let go), bit 3 mode_setup asked for.
mode ($30): 0 after power on and ACL (the time is set with left and right), 1 the clock, 2 Game B, 4 Game A, 8 the alarm's setting.
key_prev ($31): the last reading of the R4 keys (read_keys).
alarm_hr_tens ($32): the alarm's hours, tens (0 or 1), bit 3 PM; alarm_hr ($33) the hours' units, alarm_min_tens ($34) and alarm_min ($35) the minutes.
alarm_hr ($33): see alarm_hr_tens.
alarm_min_tens ($34): see alarm_hr_tens.
alarm_min ($35): see alarm_hr_tens.
hr_tens ($36): the time's hours, tens (0 or 1), bit 3 PM; hr ($37), min_tens ($38) and min ($39) as for the alarm.
hr ($37): see hr_tens.
min_tens ($38): see hr_tens.
min ($39): see hr_tens.
secs_hi ($3A): the seconds' tens.
secs_lo ($3B): the seconds' units; its bits also stand in for chance: bit 1 feeds the smoke, bit 2 stops jumps (seconds ending in 4 to 7), bit 3 lets the lower window's jumper drop.
count_hi ($40): with count_lo ($41), the seconds' count: cleared by a key and by a miss, it sends the unit back to the clock 256 seconds after a game is over (timekeep).
count_lo ($41): see count_hi.
miss_time ($43): the steps left of a miss being shown (miss_start sets 9, miss_timer counts down).
best_a_hi ($45): the best score of Game A, hundreds; best_a_mid ($46) and best_a_lo ($47) the tens and units.
best_a_mid ($46): see best_a_hi.
best_a_lo ($47): see best_a_hi.
delay ($49): passes of the wait before each step, 11 at the start and down to 4 (jump_limit).
delay_left ($4A): the passes of the wait still to go (wait).
